label: input token k during original phase (positions 2-6)
explanation: Token detector for k: fires essentially only when the input is k during the original (pre-delimiter) phase, at positions 2 through 6 (rarely and weakly at 7). Never fires at t=0/1, at t>=8, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (including when k is fed back or output). Magnitude is weakest at t=2 (about 1/4 of the per-activation mass of t=3-5) and peaks around t=3-5; the strongest examples have k at position 4. Preceding tokens, sequence length, and first token barely matter. Dev F1 0.97 (precision 0.97, recall 0.97, mass recall 0.99).

issues: Minor: the false positives cluster at t=2. When k is input at t=2 the feature fires about 90% of the time (precision 0.90), compared with about 97% overall. Precision is somewhat lower when orig(1) is in {a,b,c} (0.81), but this is a modest modulation with no clean rule, and the t=2 cases carry only about 7.6% of the activation mass.

Minor: the misses at t=7 (k input at t=7: precision 0.36, mass recall 0.007) are weak and consistent with the explanation's 'rarely and weakly at position 7'. Extending the bound to t<=7 brings recall to 0.9998 but lowers F1 to 0.962, so the t<=6 bound is the better choice.

Verified: zero activations at t=0, t=1, t>=8, on the delimiter and in the copy phase. in_tok==k accounts for 100% of the mass (only 6 non-k activations). Activation mass peaks at t=3-5 (0.29/0.31/0.22) and is low at t=2 (0.076). Sequence length L has only a mild effect (excluding L=3 changes nothing). Test scores reproduce: precision 0.974, recall 0.971, F1 0.973, mass recall 0.993.
